cues.AD-R01: Welcome aboard. Beyond Earth are worlds we know almost nothing about. What can we bring back?
cues.AD-R02: Each half-tablet has an instrument, two energy units and one archive slot. These resources aren't shared.
cues.AD-R03: First, measure. Then decide whether to intervene. Finally, choose which document to send onward. There isn't room for everything.
cues.AD-R04: You can work, or you can watch. The instruments will wait. The controls remain yours.
cues.AD-R05: Navigation, hold course. Prepare your instruments. Soon, Earth will lose sight of us.
cues.AD-R06: Ten channels are ready. Each follows something different: an outline, a resource cost, a change.
cues.AD-R07: We can't stop the journey for every question. We'll have to choose where to look more closely.
cues.AD-R08: From far away, I seem smooth all over. Bring your instrument close to one spot, and you lose the whole.
cues.AD-R09: A broad observation costs one unit. A detailed one costs two. What you save can protect the probe at our next stop.
cues.AD-R10: Look at the object on your tablet. How much of it do you want to investigate? Adjust your instrument.
cues.AD-R11: The reading is complete. Your screen shows what you kept and the energy left in reserve.
cues.AD-R12: Keep the edges beside every image. They mark the beginning of what you haven't seen.
cues.AD-R13: Your instruments are in my region now. A particle cloud will cross them. Watch it pass, or shelter your probe.
cues.AD-R14: Shelter costs one unit and leaves three seconds without a reading. Without it, the reading is complete, but noisy.
cues.AD-R15: The cloud is approaching the probe. Check your reserve. An interrupted reading and a noisy one don't tell the same story.
cues.AD-R16: You can close the probe's eye for a moment. Or leave it open through the cloud.
cues.AD-R17: The cloud has passed. If you kept a recording, the screen also shows your command.
cues.AD-R18: We keep the gaps without data too. Otherwise, the next crew may mistake the instrument's silence for the world's silence.
cues.AD-R19: I can keep everything aboard. But each channel sends just one document home. Which one will represent your expedition?
cues.AD-R20: Your tablet shows what you kept: an observation, a probe report, or an empty space. Each tells a different story.
cues.AD-R21: Those who follow us will see the documents before they see the worlds. Choose what would help them most.
cues.AD-R22: Every instrument has something to send. Look at the documents and choose one. Or leave the space empty.
cues.AD-R23: Some instruments have nothing to send. Where there are documents, choose one. Or leave the space empty.
cues.AD-R24: I'll put your chosen documents in the return package. The rest stay in the ship's memory.
cues.AD-R25: Keep the empty spaces visible too. Perhaps that's where the next expedition begins.
cues.AD-R26: The transmission is ready. The instruments can rest. We're beginning the crossing.
cues.AD-R27: Somewhere beyond this passage is home. I'm trying to remember how big it seemed the day we left.
cues.v4-saturn-01: Look at the rings! It's Saturn. We're back in the Solar System. From here, we know the way home.
cues.v4-saturn-02: From a distance, the rings look solid. Up close, they're countless pieces of ice and rock. Each one orbits Saturn.
cues.v4-saturn-03: We leave Saturn behind. Our next stop is a world of oceans, clouds and people waiting for us.
cues.AD-R28: Earth, ahead. I'm opening the return link and preparing your choices.
cues.AD-R29: Say how wide your view was, too. A narrow image isn't the whole world.
cues.AD-R30: Keep the probe's trace beside the reading. Your instrument passed through my world too.
cues.AD-R31: The ship's memory stays open. What's missing keeps its place, until another journey.
cues.AD-R32: We've watched three worlds without exhausting their mysteries. Now comes the world we thought we knew completely.
cues.AD-R33: The Earth link is open. Here is what our expedition is bringing back.
cues.AD-R34: The transmission brings two views together: what you saw, and the probe's traces. The next crew can read them together.
cues.AD-R35: You sent one type of document. Through it, the next crew will look back at our journey.
cues.AD-R36: No documents are going to Earth. What we gathered stays in the ship's memory. The journey can begin again.
cues.AD-R37: Here is our expedition's collection. What we chose to keep may begin another journey, for someone else.
cues.AD-R38: Ten slots, ten documents. The transmission is complete. And the worlds still have so much to show us.
cues.AD-R39: There are empty spaces in the transmission. We'll leave them that way. The next journey has its own questions.
cues.AD-R40: From here, our journey may begin someone else's. Thank you, crew. Stay at your stations. Your guide will tell you when to stand up.
